title: Which of 2032, 2048, 1027 and 1089 are not perfect squares?
description: The last digits rule out two numbers, and the squares on either side of the others settle the rest. The two sets of squares are used again as a check.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is a perfect square only if it ends in a possible digit and sits exactly on a square. Watch for students who see one possible last digit and decide the number is a square.

video_script.why: The child uses the last digit and the squares on either side, as in the solved example, to decide which numbers are perfect squares.
video_script.substitution: Check the last digit, then trap the number between two squares and see whether it sits on one.
video_script.anchor: four number cards, two thousand thirty two, two thousand forty eight, one thousand twenty seven and one thousand eighty nine
video_script.payoff_line: Two thousand thirty two, two thousand forty eight and one thousand twenty seven are not perfect squares

final_answer.spoken: two thousand thirty two, two thousand forty eight and one thousand twenty seven are not perfect squares, and one thousand eighty nine is thirty three squared

maths_rules: a perfect square ends in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9, so 2032 (ends in 2) and 2048 (ends in 8) are not squares
32² = 1024 and 33² = 1089, so 1024 < 1027 < 1089 and 1027 is not a square
video_script.design: One idea: last digit, then squares on either side. The four cards stay in the anchor band and the checks sit on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='digits'/>A perfect square ends only in zero, one, four, five, six or nine.
<bookmark mark='line'/>A number that is not a perfect square sits between two perfect squares.
<bookmark mark='between'/>We will use both tests.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the first two numbers are two thousand thirty two and two thousand forty eight. The others are one thousand twenty seven and one thousand eighty nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: which of the four are not perfect squares

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which of them are not perfect squares.

beats.on_screen: 2032 ends in 2 and 2048 ends in 8; a square never ends in 2 or 8, so neither is a perfect square

marks.ends: the last digits 2 of 2032 and 8 of 2048 are circled
marks.no: a cross is drawn on 2032 and on 2048

narration: <bookmark mark='ends'/>Step one, look at the last digits.
Two thousand thirty two ends in two, and two thousand forty eight ends in eight.
<bookmark mark='no'/>No perfect square ends in two or eight, so neither of them is a perfect square.

beats.on_screen: 32² = 1024 and 33² = 1089, so 1024 < 1027 < 1089 and 1027 is not a perfect square

marks.between: 1024 < 1027 < 1089 is written and 1027 is crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='near'/>Step two, trap one thousand twenty seven between squares.
Thirty two squared is one thousand twenty four, and thirty three squared is one thousand eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='between'/>One thousand twenty seven is between them, so it is not a perfect square.

beats.on_screen: 1089 sits exactly on 33², so 1089 is a perfect square

marks.on: 1089 is matched with 33² and a tick is drawn
marks.yes: the words perfect square are written under 1089

narration: <bookmark mark='on'/>Step three, look at one thousand eighty nine again.
It does not sit between two squares. It sits exactly on thirty three squared.
<bookmark mark='yes'/>This one is a perfect square.

beats.on_screen: put the answers back: 45² = 2025 and 46² = 2116, so 2025 < 2032 < 2048 < 2116

marks.back: the words check with squares on either side are written
marks.both: 2032 and 2048 are placed between them and ticked as not squares

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the answers back in the question with squares on either side.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Forty five squared is two thousand twenty five, and forty six squared is two thousand one hundred sixteen.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Both two thousand thirty two and two thousand forty eight sit between them.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (i) 2032, (ii) 2048 and (iii) 1027 are not perfect squares; 1089 = 33²
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Two thousand thirty two, two thousand forty eight and one thousand twenty seven are not perfect squares.
One thousand eighty nine is thirty three squared.
